label: Opinion (Agree/Disagree)
question_pattern: To what extent do you agree or disagree?

structure.template: Paraphrase the question + State your clear position
structure.example: It is often argued that [paraphrase topic]. I strongly agree/disagree with this view because [reason 1] and [reason 2].
tips: Never copy the question word-for-word — paraphrase it
State your opinion clearly in the last sentence
Don't list all your reasons — just hint at your direction

structure.template: Topic sentence + Explain + Example + Result + Link back
structure.example: The primary reason I support this view is that [main argument]. This is because [explanation]. For example, [specific example]. As a result, [consequence]. This clearly demonstrates that [link to thesis].
tips: Start with your strongest argument
The example should be specific, not vague
Every sentence should serve the topic sentence

structure.template: Topic sentence + Explain + Example + Result + Link back
structure.example: Furthermore, [second argument]. [Explanation of why]. A case in point is [example]. Consequently, [outcome]. This further reinforces the view that [link to thesis].
tips: Use a different connector than Body 1
This paragraph can address a counterargument and refute it
Keep the same structure for coherence

structure.template: Restate position + Final thought
structure.example: In conclusion, I firmly believe that [restate thesis]. [Final thought — recommendation, prediction, or broader implication].
tips: Never introduce new ideas in the conclusion
Don't start with 'To conclude, I conclude that...'
A strong conclusion echoes but doesn't copy your introduction

label: Discussion (Both Views)
question_pattern: Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

structure.template: Background + View A + View B + Your position (optional here)
structure.example: [Topic] is a subject of considerable debate. While some people believe that [View A], others argue that [View B]. This essay will discuss both perspectives before presenting my own view.
tips: You can state your opinion here or save it for the conclusion
Make sure you mention BOTH sides in the intro
Don't use 'some people think... other people think...' — paraphrase more naturally

structure.template: Present View A + Explain + Example + Consequence
structure.example: On the one hand, proponents of [View A] argue that [explanation]. This is primarily because [reason]. For instance, [example]. As a consequence, [result].
tips: Present this view fairly even if you disagree
Use reporting language: 'proponents argue', 'advocates claim'
Don't reveal your opinion yet

structure.template: Present View B + Explain + Example + State your preference
structure.example: On the other hand, others contend that [View B]. [Explanation]. To illustrate, [example]. In my opinion, this perspective is more compelling because [reason].
tips: This is where you align with one side
Your opinion should feel like a natural extension of the discussion
Don't sit on the fence — examiners want a clear position

structure.template: Summarise + Restate your position
structure.example: In conclusion, while both viewpoints have merit, I believe that [your position] because [key reason]. [Final thought].
tips: Acknowledge both sides briefly
Your final position should be unmistakable

label: Problem & Solution
question_pattern: What are the problems and what solutions can be suggested?

structure.template: Paraphrase the problem + State you will discuss problems and solutions
structure.example: [Topic] has become a growing concern in many parts of the world. This essay will examine the key problems associated with this issue and propose viable solutions.
tips: Don't list the problems in the intro — just introduce the topic
Keep it concise — 2 sentences max

structure.template: Problem 1 + Explain + Evidence + Problem 2 + Explain
structure.example: One of the most significant problems is [Problem 1]. This is largely due to [cause]. For example, [evidence]. Another pressing issue is [Problem 2], which has led to [consequence].
tips: Cover 2 problems — don't list 5 superficially
Explain WHY each is a problem, not just what it is
Use cause-effect connectors

structure.template: Solution 1 (matching Problem 1) + How it works + Solution 2 + Expected outcome
structure.example: To address the first issue, [Solution 1]. This would work by [mechanism]. Furthermore, [Solution 2] could tackle [Problem 2]. If implemented effectively, these measures would [positive outcome].
tips: Match each solution to a specific problem from Body 1
Explain HOW the solution works — don't just name it
Use conditional language: 'if... then...', 'this would...'

structure.template: Restate the problem + Summarise solutions + Final thought
structure.example: In conclusion, while [problem] poses serious challenges, [solutions] offer a path forward. It is essential that [who] takes action to [what].
tips: End on a forward-looking note
A recommendation works well here

label: Advantages & Disadvantages
question_pattern: What are the advantages and disadvantages of this? / Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?

structure.template: Paraphrase topic + State there are both advantages and disadvantages (+ your leaning if 'outweigh' question)
structure.example: [Topic] has become increasingly [common/controversial]. While there are clear benefits to this trend, there are also notable drawbacks. Overall, I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
tips: If the question asks 'outweigh', you MUST give your opinion
If it just asks to discuss, you can save opinion for conclusion

structure.template: Advantage 1 + Explain + Example + Advantage 2 + Explain
structure.example: The most significant advantage is [Advantage 1]. This means that [explanation]. For example, [specific case]. Additionally, [Advantage 2], which enables [positive outcome].
tips: Lead with your stronger side if it's an 'outweigh' question
2 well-developed advantages > 4 surface-level ones

structure.template: Disadvantage 1 + Explain + Example + Disadvantage 2 + Consequence
structure.example: However, there are also drawbacks to consider. The main disadvantage is [Disadvantage 1], which can lead to [negative consequence]. Furthermore, [Disadvantage 2]. This is evidenced by [example].
tips: If you think advantages outweigh, make this paragraph slightly shorter
Don't contradict your own thesis — acknowledge drawbacks but keep perspective

structure.template: Summarise + Final judgement
structure.example: In conclusion, although [disadvantages exist], the [advantages] are more significant. On balance, [your final position].
tips: 'On balance' is the perfect connector for this essay type
Your judgement should be clear and decisive

label: Two-Part Question
question_pattern: Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?

structure.template: Paraphrase + State you'll address both parts
structure.example: [Paraphrase the topic]. This essay will explore the reasons behind this trend and assess whether it is a positive or negative development.
tips: Identify the TWO distinct questions clearly
Don't answer them in the intro — just set up

structure.template: Direct answer + Reason 1 + Example + Reason 2 + Explain
structure.example: There are several reasons why [answer to Q1]. Primarily, [Reason 1]. For example, [evidence]. Another contributing factor is [Reason 2], as [explanation].
tips: Dedicate the ENTIRE paragraph to Question 1
Give 2 well-explained reasons

structure.template: Direct answer + Argument + Example + Counter + Your position
structure.example: In my view, this is largely a [positive/negative] development. This is because [argument]. To illustrate, [example]. Although some might argue that [counter], I believe [your stance].
tips: Give a clear answer — don't fence-sit
Acknowledging the other side shows balance (Band 7+)

structure.template: Summarise both answers
structure.example: In conclusion, [summary of Q1 answer], and I believe this is [positive/negative] because [key reason].
tips: Reference both questions in your conclusion
Keep it tight — 2 sentences
